definition_en: to act dishonestly in order to gain an advantage, or a person who does this
core_image: 考场上把答案写在小纸条上的人
scene: 考场里静得能听见笔尖沙沙作响。He tried to cheat in the final exam and was caught at once.
sceneCN: 这里 cheat 指「作弊」（第 1 个义项：在考试或比赛中用不正当手段取胜）；句意是他想在期末考试中作弊，当场就被抓住了。

senses.title: To trick someone for gain
senses.definition: to make someone believe something false so that you gain money or an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 让人相信假事，从而骗取钱财或好处
senses.example: The seller cheated an old couple out of their savings.
senses.exampleCN: 卖家骗走了一对老夫妇的积蓄。
senses.why: The old legal word for seizing property gave the idea of taking by unfair means.
senses.whyCN: 古老的法律用语本指夺取财产，由此生出用不正当手段取得的意思。

senses.title: To act dishonestly in a test
senses.definition: to break the rules of an exam or a game in order to do better
senses.definitionCN: 为取得更好成绩而违反考试或比赛规则
senses.example: Two students were caught cheating in the midterm.
senses.exampleCN: 两名学生在期中考试中被发现作弊。
senses.why: The general sense of unfair gain narrowed to unfair gain inside a contest.
senses.whyCN: 一般意义上的不义之财缩小为比赛内部的不正当获利。

senses.title: A dishonest person
senses.definition: a person who deceives others, or a single act of deception
senses.definitionCN: 欺骗他人的人，也指一次欺骗行为
senses.example: He turned out to be a cheat who sold fake tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 原来他是个卖假票的骗子。
senses.why: English often turns an action verb into a noun that names the person who does it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把动作动词转成名词，用来指做这件事的人。

intro.en: Cheat is a worn-down legal word that once meant land falling back to a lord.
intro.cn: cheat 是一个磨短的法律词，原本指归回领主的土地。

items.en: Excadere meant to fall out or fall away.
items.cn: 拉丁语 excadere 意为脱落、掉出。

items.en: Excadere named property that fell back to a lord for want of heirs.
items.cn: 该词在中世纪拉丁语中指因无继承人而归回领主的财产。

items.en: Escheat carried that legal sense into French.
items.cn: escheat 把这个法律含义带进法语。

items.en: The shortened form cheat first meant to seize property by such a claim.
items.cn: 缩略形式 cheat 最初指以这类名目夺取财产。

items.en: The sense widened to any dishonest gain, then to a dishonest person.
items.cn: 词义扩展到一切不义之财，再转指行骗的人。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps a short similar spelling, while the meaning group names acts of dishonesty.
note.cn: 形近组共享相近的短拼写，近义组列出各种不诚实的行为。

entries.definition: low in price or poor in quality
the front part of the body below the neck
a solid food made from milk
entries.definitionCN: 用牛奶制成的固体食物

entries.definition: to make someone believe something untrue
to fool someone by a clever plan
the crime of gaining money by lying

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the cheap look-alike, the old escheat and the three fixed prepositions.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用形近词 cheap、古词 escheat 以及三个固定介词。

normal.en: Cheat and cheap differ by one letter: a cheat sells you something cheap and fake.
normal.cn: cheat 与 cheap 只差一个字母：骗子卖给你便宜却虚假的东西。

normal.en: The old word escheat meant land falling back to a lord; cheat is that word worn down.
normal.cn: 古词 escheat 指土地归回领主，cheat 就是它磨短后的样子。

normal.en: Cheat in an exam, cheat at cards, cheat on a test: each preposition marks its own scene.
normal.cn: cheat in an exam、cheat at cards、cheat on a test，每个介词都标出自己的场景。

normal.en: A cheat is a person and cheating is the act, while cheater is the plain agent noun.
normal.cn: a cheat 指人，cheating 指行为，cheater 则是最直白的施动名词。

normal.en: Cheat death is the one flattering phrase: it means to escape death narrowly.
normal.cn: cheat death 是唯一带褒义的搭配，意为死里逃生。

abstract.en: Picture a corner of a small answer note slipping out of a sleeve.
abstract.cn: 想象一小角答案纸条从袖口滑出来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand swapping one card under a card table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在牌桌下换掉一张牌。

abstract.en: Picture a man whispering low prices for fake tickets at a station gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一个男人在车站门口低声兜售假票。

examples.en: He cheated the company out of a large sum.
examples.cn: 他骗走了公司一大笔钱。

examples.en: The teacher warned us never to cheat.
examples.cn: 老师警告我们绝不要作弊。

examples.en: A cheat never keeps friends for long.
examples.cn: 骗子留不住朋友。

dict_mnemonic.text: cheat 与 cheap 只差一个字母：便宜货里最容易藏着骗局。

root: 源自拉丁语 excadere（脱落），经中世纪拉丁语与古法语 escheat（无嗣归公的土地）缩略为 cheat，本指以不正当名目取得财产。

sensesIntro.en: The seizure of property gives the general sense of dishonest gain, which narrows to exam rooms and then shifts to the person.
sensesIntro.cn: 对财产的夺取给出「不义之财」的总义，随后缩小到考场，最后转到行骗的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand hiding an answer note inside a sleeve.
core.cn: 核心意象：把答案纸条藏在袖子里的那只手。

branches.en: A seller takes money by telling a lie.
branches.cn: 卖家靠说谎拿走钱财。

branches.en: The exam room is where the unfair gain happens.
branches.cn: 考场是不正当获利发生的场所。

branches.en: The same word then names the person who lies.
branches.cn: 同一个词随后指说谎的那个人。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of a hidden unfair move.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「暗中不正当操作」的意思。

branches.en: Cheating in a test earns the label cheat.
branches.cn: 在考试中作弊就会得到 cheat 这个称呼。

intro.en: One short root serves the verb, the noun and every derived form of cheat.
intro.cn: 一个短词根支撑 cheat 的动词、名词与全部派生形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin excadere and Old French escheat stand behind the modern word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 excadere 与古法语 escheat 是现代这个词的前身。

items.example: They cheated on the last quiz.
The cheated buyers sued the shop.
items.exampleCN: 受骗的买家起诉了这家店。

items.example: Escheat was a medieval legal term.
items.exampleCN: escheat 是中世纪的法律术语。

latinEntries.meaning: to fall out or fall away
latinEntries.example: Excadere is the remote base of cheat.
latinEntries.exampleCN: excadere 是 cheat 的远源词基。

latinEntries.meaning: property falling back to a lord
latinEntries.example: Escheat lost its first sound to become cheat.
latinEntries.exampleCN: escheat 丢掉首音后变成 cheat。

definition_en: to examine something to make sure it is correct or safe, or an examination of this kind
core_image: 拿着一份清单逐项打勾的手
scene: 出发前屋里还亮着灯。She checked the list twice before leaving the house.
sceneCN: 这里 check 指「核对」（第 1 个义项：逐项查看是否正确）；句意是她出门前把清单核对了两遍。

senses.title: To examine and confirm
senses.definition: to look at something carefully in order to see whether it is correct or safe
senses.definitionCN: 仔细查看某物，判断其是否正确或安全
senses.example: Please check your answers before handing in the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 交卷之前请核对你的答案。
senses.why: A chess warning asked a player to look at the board at once, and looking closely became the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 棋盘上的警告要求棋手立刻查看局势，仔细查看便成了核心义。

senses.title: To stop or slow something
senses.definition: to stop or slow the progress of something harmful
senses.definitionCN: 阻止或减缓有害事物的发展
senses.example: The new rules are meant to check the spread of the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定旨在阻止火势蔓延。
senses.why: Blocking the king in chess turned into the general idea of holding something back.
senses.whyCN: 在国际象棋中挡住国王，转化为一般意义上的「拦住」。

senses.title: A bank order
senses.definition: a printed order telling a bank to pay money from an account
senses.definitionCN: 指示银行从账户付款的印刷单据
senses.example: He paid the rent by check.
senses.exampleCN: 他用支票付了房租。
senses.why: The word also named a written order that could be checked against a bank account.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也指可向银行账户核对兑现的书面命令。

intro.en: Check began as the chess cry that warned a king he was in danger.
intro.cn: check 最初是国际象棋里提醒国王处境危险的一声喊。

items.en: Shah meant king.
items.cn: 波斯语 shah 意为国王。

items.en: The cry al-shah warned that the king was threatened.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语中的喊声提示国王受到威胁。

items.en: Eschec named the chess move that attacked the king.
items.cn: 古法语 eschec 指攻击国王的那一步棋。

items.en: English check first meant a chess threat to the king.
items.cn: 英语 check 最初指棋局中对国王的威胁。

items.en: The word widened to any sudden stop, then to inspection and to a bank order.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何突然的制止，再扩展到查看与银行票据。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one sound or one letter, while the meaning group lists acts of careful looking.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个音或一个字母，近义组列出仔细查看的动作。

entries.definition: a bank order spelled the British way
entries.definitionCN: 英式拼写的银行付款单

entries.definition: the side of the face below the eye
a board game of kings and queens
entries.definitionCN: 以国王与王后为棋子的棋盘游戏

entries.definition: to look at something in detail
to look at something officially for faults
to prove that something is true

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the chess origin, three everyday phrases with check and the British spelling cheque.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用国际象棋来源、三个含 check 的日常搭配以及英式拼写 cheque。

normal.en: The chess word check shouted that a king was in danger, and English kept the shout.
normal.cn: 国际象棋里的 check 高喊国王有危险，英语把这声喊留了下来。

normal.en: Check the list, check in, check out: three daily phrases all involve confirming something.
normal.cn: check the list、check in、check out，三个日常搭配都涉及确认。

normal.en: Cheque is the British spelling of the same sound, used only for the bank order.
normal.cn: cheque 是同一读音的英式拼写，只用于银行付款单。

normal.en: To check a fire is to hold it back, the old chess sense of blocking a king.
normal.cn: to check a fire 是把火拦住，正是旧日棋局中挡住国王的意思。

normal.en: Checklist and check-in are compounds built directly from the verb stem.
normal.cn: checklist 与 check-in 都是直接从动词词干构成的复合词。

abstract.en: Picture a finger moving down a paper list, ticking one line at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指沿纸上的清单下移，一行行打勾。

abstract.en: Picture a chess piece halted just before it reaches the king.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚棋子冲到国王面前却被挡住。

abstract.en: Picture a bank clerk sliding a printed slip across a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象银行职员把一张印刷单据从柜台推过来。

examples.en: She checked the door twice before going to bed.
examples.cn: 她睡前把门检查了两遍。

examples.en: The doctor will check your eyes tomorrow.
examples.cn: 医生明天会检查你的眼睛。

examples.en: A firm answer can check a rumour at once.
examples.cn: 坚定的答复能立刻止住谣言。

dict_mnemonic.text: check 与 chess 同源：棋盘上一声「将军」，就是把对方的行动拦下来。

root: 源自波斯语 shah（国王），经阿拉伯语与古法语 eschec 进入英语，本为国际象棋中「将军」的警告声。

sensesIntro.en: The warning cry gives the idea of a sudden stop, which splits into careful looking and into holding something back.
sensesIntro.cn: 警告的喊声给出「突然制止」的意思，随后分出仔细查看与加以拦阻两条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice calling out that the king must be watched.
core.cn: 核心意象：一声喊出「看好国王」的提醒。

branches.en: Looking closely grew out of the demand to watch the board.
branches.cn: 仔细查看源自「看好棋盘」的要求。

branches.en: Stopping a fire repeats the old blocking move.
branches.cn: 阻止火势沿用了旧日拦挡的动作。

branches.en: A bank order is checked against an account before it is paid.
branches.cn: 银行票据付款前要对着账户核对。

branches.en: Both senses keep the energy of a sudden halt.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留了「骤然停住」的力度。

branches.en: Inspection and the paper order share one written word.
branches.cn: 查看与纸质票据共用一个书写形式。

intro.en: Check stays a single short stem across its verb, noun and compound forms.
intro.cn: check 在动词、名词与复合形式中始终保持同一个短词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem reaches back through Old French eschec to Persian shah, the word for a king.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干经古法语 eschec 上溯到波斯语 shah，即国王。

items.example: She is checking the list now.
The pilot ran through the checklist.

items.exampleCN: 检查员发现了一个错误。

items.meaning: the act of registering on arrival

items.example: She wrote a cheque for the rent.
items.exampleCN: 她开了一张付房租的支票。

latinEntries.meaning: the chess threat to a king
latinEntries.example: Eschec entered English as check.
latinEntries.exampleCN: eschec 进入英语后写作 check。

latinEntries.example: Shah is the oldest layer of check.
latinEntries.exampleCN: shah 是 check 最古老的一层。

definition_en: the soft side of the face below the eye, or bold rudeness that shows no shame
core_image: 笑起来鼓起的两侧脸颊
scene: 屋里忽然安静下来，孩子低着头。A tear ran down her cheek when she heard the news.
sceneCN: 这里 cheek 指「脸颊」（第 1 个义项：眼睛下方的面部侧面）；句意是她听到消息时一滴泪顺着脸颊流了下来。

collocations.zh: 挨了打还把另一边脸转过去

senses.title: The side of the face
senses.definition: the soft part of the face on either side below the eye
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛下方脸两侧柔软的部分
senses.example: A tear rolled down his cheek.
senses.exampleCN: 一滴泪顺着他的脸颊滚落。
senses.why: Old English used the word for the jaw, and the meaning later moved to the soft side of the face.
senses.whyCN: 古英语用这个词指颌骨，后来意义移到面部柔软的一侧。

senses.title: Bold rudeness
senses.definition: rude boldness that shows no shame or respect
senses.definitionCN: 毫无羞耻与敬意的放肆无礼
senses.example: He had the cheek to ask for more money.
senses.exampleCN: 他竟然有脸再要钱。
senses.why: A person without shame does not blush, so the word for the face came to mean impudence.
senses.whyCN: 不知羞耻的人不会脸红，于是表示「脸」的词也用来表示放肆。

intro.en: Cheek began as a word for the jaw and slid upward to the soft side of the face.
intro.cn: cheek 起初指颌骨，后来向上移到面部柔软的一侧。

items.en: A root kau- named the jaw and the act of chewing.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词根 kau- 指颌骨与咀嚼的动作。

items.en: Ceace named the jaw and the bony side of the face.
items.cn: 古英语 ceace 指颌骨与面部骨性的一侧。

items.en: Cheke shifted to the soft flesh below the eye.
items.cn: cheke 的意义移到眼睛下方的柔软皮肉。

items.en: The word gained a second sense of bold rudeness.
items.cn: 这个词获得了「放肆无礼」的第二个义项。

items.en: Cheek now covers anatomy, manners and many fixed phrases.
items.cn: 如今 cheek 涵盖身体部位、举止以及大量固定搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same opening sound, while the meaning group names the face and boldness.
note.cn: 形近组共享相同的开头音，近义组列出面部与放肆的说法。

entries.definition: to examine something closely
a solid food made from milk
entries.definitionCN: 用牛奶制成的固体食物

entries.definition: low in price or poor in quality
either of the bones that hold the teeth
boldness that others find rude
entries.definitionCN: 被别人视为无礼的大胆

entries.definition: fearless rudeness

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the jaw root, the chewing link and the idiom about turning the other cheek.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用颌骨词根、咀嚼联系以及「转过另一边脸」的习语。

normal.en: Cheek once meant jaw, and the jaw muscle moves whenever you chew.
normal.cn: cheek 曾指颌骨，而咀嚼时动的正是颌部的肌肉。

normal.en: The plural cheeks simply adds an s to the soft side of the face.
normal.cn: 复数 cheeks 只是在表示面颊的词后加 s。

normal.en: Turn the other cheek is the famous phrase: it means to answer harm with patience.
normal.cn: turn the other cheek 是著名说法，意为以忍耐回应伤害。

normal.en: Cheek to cheek describes two dancers held close together.
normal.cn: cheek to cheek 形容两个舞者贴得很近。

normal.en: The same word turns abstract in have the cheek, which means to be boldly rude.
normal.cn: 同一个词在 have the cheek 中变得抽象，意为厚着脸皮。

abstract.en: Picture two red patches on a child's face after a long run.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子长跑之后脸上两团红。

abstract.en: Picture a tear stopping halfway down a still face.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴泪停在静止的脸颊中间。

abstract.en: Picture someone smiling calmly after being refused twice.
abstract.cn: 想象某人被拒绝两次后仍平静地笑着。

examples.en: Her cheeks went red when the teacher praised her.
examples.cn: 老师表扬她时，她的脸颊红了。

examples.en: He kissed his mother on the cheek and left.
examples.cn: 他亲了亲母亲的脸颊就走了。

examples.en: She had the cheek to blame the whole team.
examples.cn: 她竟有脸把责任推给整个团队。

dict_mnemonic.text: cheek 与 chew 同源：咀嚼时一鼓一鼓的地方，就是脸颊。

root: 源自日耳曼语词根 kau-（颌骨、咀嚼），古英语作 ceace，中古英语 cheke 转指眼睛下方的面颊。

sensesIntro.en: The jaw word climbs to the soft side of the face, and from the face it reaches the idea of shameless boldness.
sensesIntro.cn: 表示颌骨的词上移到面部柔软处，再由「脸」引申出不知羞耻的放肆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the soft curve of a face beside the smile.
core.cn: 核心意象：笑容旁边那一道柔软的脸部弧线。

branches.en: The physical cheek sits below the eye.
branches.cn: 实体的脸颊位于眼睛下方。

branches.en: The abstract sense names bold disrespect.
branches.cn: 抽象义指大胆无礼。

branches.en: Kissing on the cheek marks affection.
branches.cn: 亲脸颊表示亲近。

branches.en: The face word lends itself to idioms about shame.
branches.cn: 表示脸的词自然延伸出关于羞耻的习语。

branches.en: Having the cheek means lacking all shame.
branches.cn: have the cheek 意为毫无羞耻。

intro.en: Cheek builds a small family from one Old English stem.
intro.cn: cheek 由一个古英语词干构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic rather than Latin, and it links to the word for chewing.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，并与表示咀嚼的词相连。

items.example: Her cheek was warm to the touch.
items.exampleCN: 她的脸颊摸上去是温的。

items.example: His cheeks were red from the cold.

items.exampleCN: 那个调皮的男孩顶了嘴。

items.meaning: in a rude but playful way
items.example: He grinned cheekily at the guard.

items.meaning: to crush food with the teeth

latinEntries.example: Ceace is the oldest recorded form of cheek.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ceace 是 cheek 有记录的最古形式。

definition_zh: 快乐的；开朗的；令人愉快的
definition_en: showing happiness in the way you look and behave, or making a place feel bright and pleasant
core_image: 清晨拉开窗帘、回头笑着打招呼的人
scene: 清晨的阳光照进厨房。She gave a cheerful greeting to everyone at the table.
sceneCN: 这里 cheerful 指「开朗的」（第 1 个义项：神情举止显出快乐）；句意是她向桌边每个人愉快地打招呼。

pos.zh: 快乐的；开朗的；令人愉快的

senses.title: Happy in manner
senses.definition: showing a bright and happy manner in the way you look, speak or act
senses.definitionCN: 在神情、言语或举止上显出明朗的快乐
senses.example: He stayed cheerful even during the long delay.
senses.exampleCN: 即使长时间延误，他依然开朗。
senses.why: The old word for the face gave the idea of a bright expression, and -ful added abundance.
senses.whyCN: 古时表示「脸」的词给出明朗表情的意思，后缀 -ful 表示充满。

senses.title: Bright and pleasant
senses.definition: making a place or thing feel warm, bright and pleasant
senses.definitionCN: 使某地或某物显得温暖、明亮、宜人
senses.example: The kitchen was painted in cheerful yellow.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房刷成了明快的黄色。
senses.why: A person with a bright face makes a room feel brighter, so objects borrowed the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 面庞明朗的人让房间也变亮，于是物品借用了同一个形容词。

intro.en: Cheerful joins the old word for a face to a suffix meaning full of.
intro.cn: cheerful 把古时表示「脸」的词与表示「充满」的后缀结合在一起。

items.en: Kara named the head or the face.
items.cn: 希腊语 kara 指头或脸。

items.en: Cara named the face.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cara 指脸。

items.en: Chiere meant the look carried on a face.
items.cn: 古法语 chiere 指脸上呈现的神情。

items.en: Cheer first meant the face and its expression.
items.cn: 英语 cheer 最初指脸及其表情。

items.en: A bright face gave the sense of gladness, and -ful made cheerful.
items.cn: 明朗的脸给出喜悦之义，加上 -ful 便构成 cheerful。

note.en: The look-alike group grows from cheer, while the meaning group names happy and sunny moods.
note.cn: 形近组由 cheer 派生，近义组列出快乐与阳光的情绪词。

entries.definition: to shout in support of a team
the shouts of a supporting crowd
gloomy and without comfort
feeling or showing pleasure
pleased about something that has happened
entries.definitionCN: 为已发生的事感到高兴

entries.definition: bright and cheerful in character

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the face origin, the -ful suffix and the colour sense of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「脸」的来源、后缀 -ful 以及这个词的色彩义。

normal.en: Cheer first meant a face, so cheerful is simply a face full of light.
normal.cn: cheer 最初指脸，所以 cheerful 就是一张充满光亮的脸。

normal.en: The suffix -ful means full of, as in helpful and hopeful.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ful 意为充满，如 helpful 与 hopeful。

normal.en: Cheerful people smile at small things; cheerful rooms use warm colours.
normal.cn: cheerful 的人为小事微笑，cheerful 的房间用暖色调。

normal.en: The adverb cheerfully adds -ly and keeps the same bright meaning.
normal.cn: 副词 cheerfully 加 -ly，明朗的含义保持不变。

normal.en: Compare cheerful and cheerless: one fills a room, the other empties it.
normal.cn: 对比 cheerful 与 cheerless：一个把房间填满，一个把它掏空。

abstract.en: Picture curtains pulled open on a bright kitchen table.
abstract.cn: 想象明亮的厨房里窗帘被一把拉开。

abstract.en: Picture a waiter humming while he carries four plates.
abstract.cn: 想象服务员端着四个盘子还哼着歌。

abstract.en: Picture a yellow wall warming a room on a grey day.
abstract.cn: 想象阴沉日子里一面黄墙把房间照亮。

examples.en: She is always cheerful, even on Monday mornings.
examples.cn: 她总是很快乐，连周一早上也一样。

examples.en: The cheerful colours made the small room feel larger.
examples.cn: 明快的色彩让这个小房间显得更大。

examples.en: His cheerful voice lifted the whole group.
examples.cn: 他欢快的嗓音让整组人都振作起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: cheer 本指「脸」，加 -ful 表示「满脸都是」：一张满脸是笑的脸，就是开朗。

root: 由 cheer（源自古法语 chiere，脸、神情，再上溯拉丁语 cara 脸）加形容词后缀 -ful（充满）构成。

sensesIntro.en: A bright face gives the personal sense first, and then the brightness is transferred to rooms and colours.
sensesIntro.cn: 明朗的脸先给出形容人的义项，随后这份明亮被转移到房间与色彩上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face full of light turned toward other people.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张朝向他人、满是光亮的面孔。

branches.en: A person keeps a bright manner through trouble.
branches.cn: 一个人遇到麻烦仍保持明朗举止。

branches.en: Colours and rooms borrow the same brightness.
branches.cn: 色彩与房间借用了同一种明亮。

branches.en: The adverb cheerfully describes how the manner shows.
branches.cn: 副词 cheerfully 描述这种举止如何表现。

branches.en: Both senses rest on the image of light on a face.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在「脸上的光」这一意象上。

branches.en: A cheerful yellow wall warms a grey day.
branches.cn: 明快的黄墙让阴沉的日子变暖。

intro.en: Cheerful is a base adjective with a small but busy family of forms.
intro.cn: cheerful 是基础形容词，拥有一个不大但活跃的词形家族。

latinIntro.en: The stem comes from Latin cara, a face, by way of Old French chiere.
latinIntro.cn: 词干经古法语 chiere 上溯拉丁语 cara，意为脸。

items.example: She is the most cheerful of the three.
Her cheerfulness spread through the room.
items.exampleCN: 她的开朗传遍整个房间。

items.example: The hall felt cheerless and cold.

latinEntries.example: Cara passed into French as chiere.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cara 进入法语后写作 chiere。

latinEntries.example: Chiere became English cheer.
latinEntries.exampleCN: chiere 变成英语的 cheer。

definition_en: in a happy and bright way, or willingly and without complaint
core_image: 一边搬东西一边哼歌的人
scene: 雨下了一整天，店里却没人抱怨。The staff cheerfully carried the boxes up the stairs in the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 cheerfully 指「愉快地」（第 1 个义项：以快乐明朗的方式做事）；句意是员工们冒雨把箱子愉快地搬上楼。

senses.title: In a happy manner
senses.definition: in a way that shows a bright and happy mood
senses.definitionCN: 以显出明朗快乐情绪的方式
senses.example: She cheerfully waved at the children.
senses.exampleCN: 她愉快地朝孩子们挥手。
senses.why: The adverb adds -ly to cheerful, so the bright manner of the adjective becomes the manner of an action.
senses.whyCN: 副词在 cheerful 后加 -ly，形容词的明朗神情便成了动作的方式。

senses.title: Willingly and without complaint
senses.definition: readily and with good humour, even when the task is hard
senses.definitionCN: 即使任务艰难也乐意而带着好心情地做
senses.example: He cheerfully took the night shift for a sick colleague.
senses.exampleCN: 他爽快地替生病的同事上了夜班。
senses.why: A bright face also signals consent, so the adverb came to mean willing agreement.
senses.whyCN: 明朗的神情也传递应允，因此这个副词也表示乐意同意。

intro.en: Cheerfully is cheerful plus the native adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: cheerfully 是 cheerful 加上本土副词词尾 -ly。

items.en: Cara named the face.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cara 指脸。

items.en: Chiere meant the expression worn on a face.
items.cn: 古法语 chiere 指脸上带着的神情。

items.en: Cheer named the face and its look.
items.cn: 英语 cheer 指脸及其神情。

items.en: Cheerful added -ful, and -ly then turned it into an adverb.
items.cn: cheerful 加上 -ful，副词词尾 -ly 再把它变成副词。

items.en: Cheerfully now covers both a happy manner and willing consent.
items.cn: 如今 cheerfully 既指愉快的方式，也指乐意的应允。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cheer stem, while the meaning group lists adverbs of glad consent.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cheer 词干，近义组列出表示乐意与高兴的副词。

entries.definition: happy and bright in manner
the state of being cheerful
gloomy and without comfort
with pleasure and willingness
in a pleased and contented way
without being forced or persuaded

normalIntro.en: These hooks unpack the three pieces cheerful, -ful and -ly, then link the willing sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子拆开 cheerful、-ful 与 -ly 三段，再联系「乐意」的义项。

normal.en: Cheerfully is a three-storey word: cheer, then -ful, then -ly.
normal.cn: cheerfully 是三层楼：先 cheer，再 -ful，最后 -ly。

normal.en: The adverb answers how: how did she answer? She answered cheerfully.
normal.cn: 这个副词回答「怎样」：她怎样回答？她愉快地回答。

normal.en: Cheerfully before a verb often hints at willingness, as in cheerfully agree.
normal.cn: cheerfully 放在动词前常暗示乐意，如 cheerfully agree。

normal.en: Drop -ly and you are back to the adjective cheerful.
normal.cn: 去掉 -ly，就回到形容词 cheerful。

normal.en: The opposite manner is described by cheerlessly, a rare but regular form.
normal.cn: 相反的方式可用 cheerlessly 描述，虽少见但合乎构词规则。

abstract.en: Picture a worker carrying two heavy boxes and still humming.
abstract.cn: 想象一个工人抱着两只重箱子还在哼歌。

abstract.en: Picture a nurse answering a night bell with a smile.
abstract.cn: 想象护士带着微笑回应夜里的呼叫铃。

abstract.en: Picture rain running off a coat while its owner laughs.
abstract.cn: 想象雨水从外套上流下，而穿外套的人却在笑。

examples.en: The children cheerfully sang the whole way home.
examples.cn: 孩子们一路愉快地唱着歌回家。

examples.en: She cheerfully agreed to show us around.
examples.cn: 她爽快地答应带我们四处看看。

examples.en: He cheerfully admitted that the plan had failed.
examples.cn: 他坦然地承认计划失败了。

dict_mnemonic.text: cheerful 加 -ly：一张满脸是笑的脸做出来的动作，就是愉快地。

root: 由形容词 cheerful（cheer 脸、神情，加 -ful 充满）再加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb first describes a happy manner, and then that bright face is read as willing consent.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词先描述愉快的方式，随后那副明朗神情被理解为乐意的应允。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smile carried into a task that is not easy.
core.cn: 核心意象：把笑容带进一件并不轻松的任务里。

branches.en: The adverb describes how someone smiles or sings.
branches.cn: 这个副词描述某人怎样微笑或唱歌。

branches.en: The same form marks ready agreement to a hard task.
branches.cn: 同一形式标记出对艰难任务的欣然接受。

branches.en: It usually sits after the verb or before the verb phrase.
branches.cn: 它通常放在动词后或动词短语前。

branches.en: Both senses carry the same outward brightness.
branches.cn: 两个义项都带着同一种外露的明亮。

branches.en: A cheerful yes is a promise without complaint.
branches.cn: 一个愉快的「好」就是不带抱怨的承诺。

intro.en: Cheerfully stacks a root, a suffix and an adverb ending in a single word.
intro.cn: cheerfully 在一个词里叠起词根、后缀与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root reaches Latin cara, a face, through Old French chiere.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根经古法语 chiere 上溯拉丁语 cara，意为脸。

items.meaning: in a bright and willing way

latinEntries.example: Cara is the oldest layer of the stem.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cara 是这个词干最古老的一层。

latinEntries.example: Chiere gave English the word cheer.
latinEntries.exampleCN: chiere 给英语提供了 cheer 这个词。

definition_en: a solid food made from milk and pressed into blocks or wheels
core_image: 一块切开、露出小孔的黄色奶酪
scene: 面包刚出炉，桌上摆着一小盘切好的奶酪。He cut a thin slice of cheese for the child.
sceneCN: 这里 cheese 指「奶酪」（第 1 个义项：用牛奶制成的固体食品）；句意是他给孩子切了一薄片奶酪。

senses.title: The dairy food
senses.definition: a solid food made from milk and pressed into blocks or wheels
senses.definitionCN: 用牛奶制成、压成块或轮的固体食品
senses.example: This cheese is made from goat's milk.
senses.exampleCN: 这种奶酪是用羊奶做的。
senses.why: The word came straight from Latin caseus, the name of the food itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词直接来自拉丁语 caseus，正是这种食物本身的名称。

senses.title: The photographer's call
senses.definition: a word said to make people smile before a photograph is taken
senses.definitionCN: 拍照前让人露出笑容时喊的口令
senses.example: The photographer asked us to say cheese.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师让我们喊「茄子」。
senses.why: The long vowel forces the mouth into a smile, so the food word became a studio call.
senses.whyCN: 长元音迫使嘴形拉成微笑，于是这个食物词成了摄影棚里的口令。

intro.en: Cheese is one of the oldest Latin loanwords in English, taken from caseus.
intro.cn: cheese 是英语中最古老的拉丁语借词之一，来自 caseus。

items.en: Caseus named cheese.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caseus 指奶酪。

items.en: West Germanic speakers borrowed the word as kasjus.
items.cn: 西日耳曼语使用者把它借入，作 kasjus。

items.en: Cese named the food on the table.
items.cn: 古英语 cese 指桌上的这种食物。

items.en: The spelling settled as chese and then cheese.
items.cn: 拼写先固定为 chese，后又变成 cheese。

items.en: The word now names hundreds of kinds and also the call for a smile.
items.cn: 如今这个词指数百个品种，也指拍照时的微笑口令。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same opening sound, while the meaning group lists other dairy foods.
note.cn: 形近组共享相同的开头音，近义组列出其他奶制品。

entries.definition: a board game of kings and queens
entries.definitionCN: 以国王与王后为棋子的棋盘游戏

entries.definition: the side of the face below the eye
to run after someone quickly
a soft yellow food made from cream
entries.definitionCN: 用奶油制成的黄色软食

entries.definition: a thick food made from fermented milk
entries.definitionCN: 用发酵牛奶制成的浓稠食品

entries.definition: the thick fatty part of milk
entries.definitionCN: 牛奶中浓稠含脂的部分

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin source, the shape of the food and the photographer's call.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用拉丁语来源、食物形状以及拍照口令。

normal.en: Cheese and casein share a root: casein is the milk protein that makes cheese firm.
normal.cn: cheese 与 casein 同根：酪蛋白正是让奶酪变硬的那种牛奶蛋白。

normal.en: Say cheese: the long vowel pulls the mouth into a smile.
normal.cn: say cheese：长元音把嘴角拉成一个笑。

normal.en: Cheese is usually uncountable, but cheeses means several kinds.
normal.cn: cheese 通常不可数，而 cheeses 指好几个品种。

normal.en: Cheesy first meant like cheese, then came to mean cheap and sentimental.
normal.cn: cheesy 先指「像奶酪的」，后来指廉价而煽情。

normal.en: Cheeseburger and cheesecake are compounds that keep the food word whole.
normal.cn: cheeseburger 与 cheesecake 都是保留食物原词的复合词。

abstract.en: Picture a yellow wheel of cheese with one wedge removed.
abstract.cn: 想象一只黄色奶酪轮被切走一角。

abstract.en: Picture a knife pulling a thin slice away from a block.
abstract.cn: 想象刀从整块奶酪上片下薄薄一片。

abstract.en: Picture a family holding a smile while a camera clicks.
abstract.cn: 想象一家人保持笑容，相机咔嚓一响。

examples.en: Cheese is made by curdling milk.
examples.cn: 奶酪是通过让牛奶凝结制成的。

examples.en: He bought three kinds of cheese for the party.
examples.cn: 他为聚会买了三种奶酪。

examples.en: The children shouted cheese as the camera flashed.
examples.cn: 相机闪光时孩子们喊着「茄子」。

dict_mnemonic.text: cheese 与 chess 只差一个字母：棋盘旁的桌子上，常摆着一块奶酪。

root: 源自拉丁语 caseus（奶酪），由西日耳曼语借入，古英语作 cese，中古英语拼作 chese。

sensesIntro.en: The food sense is the original one, and the studio call grew out of the shape the word forces on the mouth.
sensesIntro.cn: 食物义是最初的义项，摄影口令则由这个词逼出的嘴形发展而来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pressed block of milk turned solid and yellow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块被压紧、凝成固体的黄色奶块。

branches.en: The basic sense names the dairy food.
branches.cn: 基本义项指这种奶制食品。

branches.en: The call makes a mouth shape, not a meal.
branches.cn: 口令只塑造嘴形，与一餐无关。

branches.en: Cheeses counts the many varieties.
branches.cn: cheeses 用来数各种品种。

branches.en: Both senses hang on the same long vowel.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依附于同一个长元音。

branches.en: The call is used only before a camera.
branches.cn: 这个口令只在相机前使用。

intro.en: Cheese keeps one short stem through its compounds and derived adjective.
intro.cn: cheese 在其复合词与派生形容词中保留同一个短词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin caseus is the source, and the same stem appears in casein, the milk protein.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caseus 是来源，同一词干也出现在表示酪蛋白的 casein 中。

items.meaning: a solid food made from milk
items.meaningCN: 用牛奶制成的固体食品

items.meaning: a burger with a cheese slice
a baked dessert of soft cheese

latinEntries.exampleCN: caseus 变成古英语的 cese。

definition_en: relating to chemistry, or a substance produced by or used in chemistry
core_image: 实验台上排成一列的试剂瓶
scene: 实验室里通风柜嗡嗡作响。The chemical reaction turned the liquid from clear to blue.
sceneCN: 这里 chemical 指「化学的」（第 1 个义项：与化学有关的）；句意是这一化学反应使液体由澄清变成蓝色。

senses.title: Relating to chemistry
senses.definition: connected with chemistry or with the substances and changes it studies
senses.definitionCN: 与化学或化学研究的物质与变化有关的
senses.example: The chemical reaction released a great deal of heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这个化学反应释放出大量热。
senses.why: The adjective was built from the old name of the art of transforming matter.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由那门「转化物质之术」的古老名称构成。

senses.title: A substance made by chemistry
senses.definition: a substance produced by or used in chemical processes
senses.definitionCN: 由化学过程产生或用于化学过程的物质
senses.example: Farmers must store chemicals away from water.
senses.exampleCN: 农民必须把化学制品存放在远离水源的地方。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun for the things it describes, a common shift in English.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成名词，指它所描述的东西，这在英语中很常见。

intro.en: Chemical descends from the old art of alchemy, whose name travelled through Arabic.
intro.cn: chemical 源自古老的炼金术，其名称经阿拉伯语辗转而来。

items.en: Khemeia named the art of transforming metals.
items.cn: 希腊语 khemeia 指转化金属的技艺。

items.en: Al-kimiya carried that art into Arabic learning.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 把这门技艺带入阿拉伯学术。

items.en: Alchimia named the same art in Europe.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alchimia 在欧洲指同一门技艺。

items.en: Chemical first meant belonging to this art.
items.cn: chemical 最初意为属于这门技艺的。

items.en: The word now covers the science itself and the substances it handles.
items.cn: 如今这个词既指这门科学，也指它处理的物质。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the chem- stem, while the meaning group lists things a laboratory handles.
note.cn: 形近组共享 chem- 词干，近义组列出实验室处理的东西。

entries.definition: a scientist who works with chemistry
the science of substances and their changes
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质及其变化的科学

entries.definition: belonging to the old art of alchemy
a material with particular qualities
a substance formed from two or more elements
entries.definitionCN: 由两种或多种元素形成的物质

entries.definition: made by chemical industry rather than nature
entries.definitionCN: 由化学工业而非自然生成的

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the chem- stem, the alchemy history and the everyday compound chemicals.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 chem- 词干、炼金术历史以及日常复合词 chemicals。

normal.en: Chemical, chemist and chemistry all stand on the same four letters chem.
normal.cn: chemical、chemist、chemistry 都站在同样的四个字母 chem 上。

normal.en: Chemical is the adjective, chemicals are the bottles a lab stores.
normal.cn: chemical 是形容词，chemicals 则是实验室存放的一瓶瓶东西。

normal.en: Alchemy came before chemistry; the old art hides inside the modern word.
normal.cn: 炼金术早于化学，这门古老技艺就藏在这个现代词里。

normal.en: A chemical change makes a new substance; a physical change does not.
normal.cn: 化学变化产生新物质，物理变化则不产生。

normal.en: The ending -al makes an adjective, as in medical and logical.
normal.cn: 词尾 -al 构成形容词，如 medical 与 logical。

abstract.en: Picture blue liquid climbing through a glass tube.
abstract.cn: 想象蓝色液体沿着玻璃管往上爬。

abstract.en: Picture rows of labelled bottles behind glass doors.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃门后一排排贴好标签的瓶子。

abstract.en: Picture a single drop changing a whole beaker's colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴液体改变整只烧杯的颜色。

examples.en: The factory must treat its chemical waste before release.
examples.cn: 这家工厂必须在排放前处理化学废料。

examples.en: Some chemicals are safe in small amounts.
examples.cn: 有些化学物质少量使用时是安全的。

examples.en: A chemical change cannot be undone easily.
examples.cn: 化学变化不容易逆转。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective comes from the name of an old art, and the noun then names the substances that art produced.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop that changes the colour of a whole beaker.

branches.en: The adjective describes reactions and processes.

branches.en: The plural noun names stored substances.

branches.en: Chemical change is the phrase that fixes the adjective.
branches.cn: chemical change 这一搭配固定了形容词的用法。

branches.en: The adjective and the noun differ only in ending.
branches.cn: 形容词与名词只差一个词尾。

branches.en: Harmful chemicals need careful storage.
branches.cn: 有害化学物质需要小心存放。

latinIntro.en: The stem passed from Greek khemeia through Arabic al-kimiya into medieval Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干从希腊语 khemeia 经阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 进入中世纪拉丁语。

items.meaning: relating to chemistry in living things

items.exampleCN: 生化信号控制这一过程。

latinEntries.example: Alchimia gave English the chem- stem.
latinEntries.exampleCN: alchimia 给英语提供了 chem- 词干。

latinEntries.example: Al-kimiya entered Latin as alchimia.
latinEntries.exampleCN: al-kimiya 进入拉丁语后作 alchimia。

definition_en: a scientist who studies chemistry, or a person who prepares and sells medicines
core_image: 穿白大褂在药柜前配药的人
scene: 街角那家小店的招牌已经褪色。The chemist weighed the powder and sealed it in a small bottle.
sceneCN: 这里 chemist 指「药剂师」（第 2 个义项：配制并出售药物的人）；句意是药剂师称好药粉，封进一只小瓶。

senses.title: A chemistry scientist
senses.definition: a scientist who studies the composition and behaviour of substances
senses.definitionCN: 研究物质组成与变化规律的科学家
senses.example: The chemist published a paper on new polymers.
senses.exampleCN: 这位化学家发表了一篇关于新型聚合物的论文。
senses.why: The -ist ending marks a person who practises the science named by the stem.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ist 标记出从事词干所命名那门科学的人。

senses.title: A person who sells medicines
senses.definition: a person trained to prepare and sell medicines in a shop
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、在店铺里配制并出售药物的人
senses.example: Ask the chemist before mixing these pills.
senses.exampleCN: 把这些药混着吃之前先问药剂师。
senses.why: In Britain the same trained person both studies drugs and hands them over the counter.
senses.whyCN: 在英国，同一位受过训练的人既研究药物，也在柜台后把药交给顾客。

senses.title: A shop selling medicines
senses.definition: a shop where medicines and small health goods are sold
senses.definitionCN: 出售药物与小型保健用品的店铺
senses.example: The chemist opens at eight on weekdays.
senses.exampleCN: 这家药房工作日八点开门。
senses.why: British speech shortens the chemist's shop to the chemist, so the person's name becomes the place.
senses.whyCN: 英式口语把 the chemist's shop 缩成 the chemist，人的称呼便成了地点。

intro.en: Chemist came from the same alchemy root that gave chemical and chemistry.
intro.cn: chemist 与 chemical、chemistry 同出炼金术这一词根。

items.en: Khemeia named the art of transforming metals.
items.cn: 希腊语 khemeia 指转化金属的技艺。

items.en: Al-kimiya carried the art into Arabic.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 把这门技艺带入阿拉伯语。

items.en: Alchimia named the art, and alchimista named its follower.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alchimia 指这门技艺，alchimista 指从事者。

items.en: Chemist first meant a student of this art.
items.cn: chemist 最初指这门技艺的研习者。

items.en: The word split into the scientist and the medicine seller.
items.cn: 这个词分化出科学家与卖药人两个意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the chem- stem, while the meaning group names people who handle medicines.
note.cn: 形近组共享 chem- 词干，近义组列出与药物打交道的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -ist person ending, the British shop idiom and the shared chem- stem.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用表示人的 -ist 词尾、英式店铺说法以及共同的 chem- 词干。

normal.en: Add -ist to chem and you get the person: a chemist works with chemistry.
normal.cn: 在 chem 后加 -ist 就得到那个人：chemist 与 chemistry 打交道。

normal.en: In Britain the chemist is both the scientist and the shop on the corner.
normal.cn: 在英国，chemist 既是科学家，也是街角那家药房。

normal.en: The chemist's means the shop, with the apostrophe standing for the missing word shop.
normal.cn: the chemist's 指那家店，撇号代替了省略掉的 shop 一词。

normal.en: Chemistry is the subject, chemist is the person, chemical is the adjective.
normal.cn: chemistry 是学科，chemist 是人，chemical 是形容词。

normal.en: An alchemist came first; a chemist is the modern heir of that old figure.
normal.cn: 先有 alchemist，chemist 是那位古老人物在现代的继承者。

abstract.en: Picture a white coat behind a counter of small drawers.
abstract.cn: 想象白色工作服站在一排小抽屉的柜台后。

abstract.en: Picture a hand weighing white powder on a brass scale.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在铜秤上称白色粉末。

abstract.en: Picture a hand-written label being pressed onto a brown bottle.
abstract.cn: 想象一张手写标签被贴到棕色瓶子上。

examples.en: The chemist explained how the two drugs interact.
examples.cn: 药剂师解释了这两种药如何相互作用。

examples.en: She trained as a chemist before turning to teaching.
examples.cn: 她在转行教书之前受训成为化学家。

examples.en: I bought the bandage at the chemist's on the corner.
examples.cn: 我在街角那家药房买了绷带。

dict_mnemonic.text: chem 加 -ist：跟化学打交道的人，既是化学家，也是给人配药的药剂师。

root: 源自希腊语 khemeia（转化金属之术），经阿拉伯语 al-kimiya、中世纪拉丁语 alchimista 进入英语，-ist 表示从事者。

sensesIntro.en: One trained person gives all three senses: the researcher, the dispenser and the shop where the dispenser works.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一位受过训练的人给出三个义项：研究者、配药者，以及配药者工作的店铺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trained hand measuring powder behind a counter.
core.cn: 核心意象：柜台后一只称量药粉的熟练的手。

branches.en: The scientist sense keeps the laboratory.
branches.cn: 科学家义项保留实验室场景。

branches.en: The dispenser sense moves to the counter.
branches.cn: 配药者义项转到柜台前。

branches.en: The shop sense names the place itself.
branches.cn: 店铺义项指地点本身。

branches.en: Both senses need the same chemical training.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要同样的化学训练。

branches.en: The person's name stands for the shop in British speech.
branches.cn: 在英式口语中，人的称呼代指那家店。

intro.en: Chemist is the chem- stem plus the person ending -ist.
intro.cn: chemist 是 chem- 词干加上表示人的词尾 -ist。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin alchimista, a follower of alchimia, is the direct model for chemist.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alchimista 是 chemist 的直接范本，指炼金术的从事者。

items.exampleCN: 两位化学家签署了报告。

latinEntries.example: Alchimista shortened into English chemist.

latinEntries.exampleCN: alchimia 提供了 chem- 词干。

definition_en: the science that studies substances and how they react, or a strong feeling of mutual understanding between people
core_image: 试管里两种液体相遇后变了颜色
scene: 两个人跑位交错，像早已排练过无数遍。Their chemistry on the court was obvious from the first minute.
sceneCN: 这里 chemistry 指「默契」（第 3 个义项：人与人之间自然的相互理解）；句意是他们在场上的默契从第一分钟就显而易见。

senses.title: The science of substances
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies what substances are made of and how they react
senses.definitionCN: 研究物质由什么构成以及如何反应的科学分支
senses.example: She took chemistry as her main subject.
senses.exampleCN: 她把化学作为主修科目。
senses.why: The -ry ending names a field of study or practice, so the art of the chemist became a science.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ry 表示一门学问或实践领域，于是化学家的技艺变成了一门科学。

senses.title: The makeup of a substance
senses.definition: the chemical composition or behaviour of a material
senses.definitionCN: 某种材料的化学组成或化学行为
senses.example: The chemistry of the lake changed after the spill.
senses.exampleCN: 泄漏之后湖水的化学成分发生了变化。
senses.why: The name of the science was applied to the very properties that science measures.
senses.whyCN: 这门科学的名称被用来指它所测量的那些性质本身。

senses.title: Mutual understanding
senses.definition: a natural and strong understanding between two people or within a group
senses.definitionCN: 两人之间或群体内部自然而强烈的相互理解
senses.example: The new coach built real chemistry among the players.
senses.exampleCN: 新教练在队员之间建立起了真正的默契。
senses.why: Two people who fit together seem to react like well-matched substances, so the laboratory word moved to feelings.
senses.whyCN: 彼此契合的两个人像两种相配的物质发生反应，实验室的词便移到了情感上。

intro.en: Chemistry carries the old name of alchemy, reshaped by Greek, Arabic and Latin.
intro.cn: chemistry 承载着炼金术的古老名称，经希腊语、阿拉伯语与拉丁语层层改造。

items.en: Khemeia named the art of transforming metals.
items.cn: 希腊语 khemeia 指转化金属的技艺。

items.en: Al-kimiya carried the art into Arabic science.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 把这门技艺带入阿拉伯学术。

items.en: Alchimia named the art in European schools.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alchimia 在欧洲学堂里指这门技艺。

items.en: Chemistry replaced alchemy as the name of a proper science.
items.cn: chemistry 取代 alchemy，成为一门正式科学的名称。

items.en: The word also names a material's makeup and the ease between two people.
items.cn: 这个词也指材料的成分以及两人之间的投合。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the chem- stem, while the meaning group names close bonds between people.
note.cn: 形近组共享 chem- 词干，近义组列出人与人之间的紧密联系。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -ry field ending, the alchemy history and the sports sense of chemistry.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用表示学科的 -ry 词尾、炼金术历史以及体育语境中的默契义。

normal.en: Chemist plus -ry gives the field: chemistry is what a chemist practises.
normal.cn: chemist 加 -ry 得到这门领域：chemistry 就是化学家所从事的学问。

normal.en: Alchemy came first, and chemistry is its disciplined modern child.
normal.cn: 先有炼金术，chemistry 是它受严格训练的现代孩子。

normal.en: Good chemistry between players is a bond you can almost see.
normal.cn: 球员之间良好的 chemistry 是一种几乎看得见的联系。

normal.en: Chemistry is uncountable, so it takes no plural in ordinary use.
normal.cn: chemistry 不可数，日常用法中没有复数。

normal.en: Organic chemistry studies carbon; soil chemistry studies the ground under a field.
normal.cn: 有机化学研究碳，土壤化学研究田地之下的泥土。

abstract.en: Picture two clear liquids meeting and turning deep blue.
abstract.cn: 想象两种澄清液体相遇后变成深蓝。

abstract.en: Picture two dancers turning without a word between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两个舞者一句不说却同时转身。

abstract.en: Picture a test tube warmed gently over a small flame.
abstract.cn: 想象一支试管在小火苗上缓缓加热。

examples.en: Chemistry explains why iron rusts in wet air.
examples.cn: 化学解释了铁在潮湿空气中为何生锈。

examples.en: The chemistry of the soil decides which plants thrive.
examples.cn: 土壤的化学成分决定哪些植物能长得旺。

examples.en: There was instant chemistry between the two actors.
examples.cn: 两位演员之间立刻就有了默契。

dict_mnemonic.text: chemist 加 -ry 表示学科：化学家研究的那门学问，就是化学；人和人「来反应」，就是默契。

root: 源自希腊语 khemeia（转化金属之术），经阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 与中世纪拉丁语 alchimia，十七世纪定型为 chemistry。

sensesIntro.en: The field of study gives the first sense, its measured properties give the second, and matched reactions give the figurative third.
sensesIntro.cn: 学科名称给出第一义，它测量的性质给出第二义，而相互契合的反应给出比喻性的第三义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two substances meeting and changing each other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两种物质相遇并彼此改变。

branches.en: The school subject sits in the laboratory.
branches.cn: 学科义项留在实验室里。

branches.en: The property sense measures a given sample.
branches.cn: 性质义项针对某一具体样本。

branches.en: The figurative sense moves to people who fit.
branches.cn: 比喻义项移到彼此契合的人身上。

branches.en: The science and what it measures share one name.
branches.cn: 科学与它所测量的对象共用一个名称。

branches.en: Both extend the idea of substances reacting well.
branches.cn: 两者都延伸了「物质相合」的意思。

intro.en: Chemistry joins the chem- stem to the field ending -ry.
intro.cn: chemistry 把 chem- 词干与表示学科的 -ry 词尾结合起来。

latinIntro.en: The stem descends from Greek khemeia by way of Arabic al-kimiya and Latin alchimia.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干从希腊语 khemeia 经阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 与拉丁语 alchimia 传下。

items.example: Organic chemistry fills a whole year.

latinEntries.example: Alchimia became the modern chemistry.

latinEntries.example: Khemeia is the oldest known form.
latinEntries.exampleCN: khemeia 是目前所知最古老的形式。

definition_en: a printed order telling a bank to pay a sum of money from an account
core_image: 一张写着金额并签了名的纸条
scene: 柜台前的队伍慢慢往前挪。He wrote a cheque for the full amount and handed it over.
sceneCN: 这里 cheque 指「支票」（第 1 个义项：指示银行付款的票据）；句意是他开了一张全额支票并递了过去。

senses.title: A written bank order
senses.definition: a printed form on which you write a sum and sign your name so that a bank pays that money
senses.definitionCN: 印好格式、由你填写金额并签名，让银行付出这笔钱的单据
senses.example: She paid the plumber by cheque.
senses.exampleCN: 她用支票付了水管工的钱。
senses.why: The word is a later spelling of check, fixed when the bank sense needed its own written form.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 check 后来的拼写，在银行义需要独立书写形式时固定下来。

senses.title: Freedom to act at will
senses.definition: permission to act freely, as if given a cheque with the amount left empty
senses.definitionCN: 像拿到一张金额空着的支票那样被允许自由行动
senses.example: The board gave the new director a blank cheque.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会给了新主管一张「空白支票」。
senses.why: A blank cheque lets the holder fill in any sum, so the phrase came to mean unlimited freedom.
senses.whyCN: 空白支票允许持有人填任何金额，于是这个说法表示不受限的自由。

intro.en: Cheque is the same word as check, respelled to keep the bank sense apart.
intro.cn: cheque 与 check 本是同一个词，改拼是为了把银行义区分出来。

items.en: Shah meant king.
items.cn: 波斯语 shah 意为国王。

items.en: Eschec named the chess move that threatened the king.
items.cn: 古法语 eschec 指威胁国王的那一步棋。

items.en: Check first meant a chess threat.
items.cn: 英语 check 最初指棋局中的威胁。

items.en: Check also named a written order on a bank.
items.cn: check 也用来指对银行开出的书面付款命令。

items.en: British banks fixed the spelling cheque for the money sense.
items.cn: 英国银行把表示钱的这一义项固定拼作 cheque。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same sound, while the meaning group names other written orders for money.
note.cn: 形近组读音相同，近义组列出其他书面的付款凭证。

a board game of kings and queens

entries.definitionCN: 可换取商品的印刷凭据

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the shared sound with check, the chess history and the blank cheque idiom.

normal.en: Cheque and check sound alike because they are one word with two spellings.
normal.cn: cheque 与 check 读音相同，因为它们是同一个词的两种拼写。

normal.en: The British write cheque for money and check for inspection.
normal.cn: 英国人用 cheque 表示钱，用 check 表示检查。

normal.en: The chess word check hides inside cheque: a bank order also says stop and pay.
normal.cn: 棋盘上的 check 藏在 cheque 里：一张支票也在说「停，付钱」。

normal.en: A blank cheque has an empty amount, so it stands for unlimited freedom.
normal.cn: 空白支票金额空着，因此表示不受限制的自由。

normal.en: Chequebook and cheque card are the two everyday compounds.
normal.cn: chequebook 与 cheque card 是两个日常复合词。

abstract.en: Picture a pen filling in an amount on a printed slip.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔在印刷单据上填金额。

abstract.en: Picture a signature drying at the bottom of a paper.
abstract.cn: 想象纸底的签名正在变干。

abstract.en: Picture a bank clerk stamping a slip and sliding it back.
abstract.cn: 想象银行职员盖章后把单据推回来。

examples.en: He wrote a cheque for two hundred pounds.
examples.cn: 他开了一张两百英镑的支票。

examples.en: Most shops no longer accept payment by cheque.
examples.cn: 多数商店不再接受支票付款。

examples.en: The committee handed the designer a blank cheque.
examples.cn: 委员会给了设计师全权委托。

dict_mnemonic.text: cheque 就是 check 的英式写法：把「检查」换成「付款单」，读音一点没变。

root: 与 check 同源，出自波斯语 shah（国王）、古法语 eschec（将军），十九世纪英国银行为付款票据固定拼作 cheque。

sensesIntro.en: The bank order is the literal sense, and the empty amount on a blank cheque gives the figurative sense of free action.
sensesIntro.cn: 银行付款单是字面义，空白支票上金额的空缺给出自由行动的比喻义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed slip that turns paper into money.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张签了名、把纸变成钱的单据。

branches.en: The literal sense is a payment order.
branches.cn: 字面义项是付款命令。

branches.en: The figurative sense is unlimited permission.
branches.cn: 比喻义项是不受限制的许可。

branches.en: The plural cheques counts single slips.
branches.cn: 复数 cheques 用来数一张张单据。

branches.en: Both senses rest on the same printed form.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依托同一张印刷单据。

branches.en: A blank cheque is signed but left empty.
branches.cn: 空白支票签了名却空着金额。

intro.en: Cheque keeps the short check stem in a British spelling.
intro.cn: cheque 以英式拼写保留 check 这个短词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem is not Latin at all; it reaches Persian shah through Old French eschec.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干并非拉丁语，而是经古法语 eschec 上溯波斯语 shah。

items.example: The cheque cleared in two days.
He kept the used cheques in a file.
The shop asked for a cheque card.
items.exampleCN: 商店要求出示支票保证卡。

items.meaning: the same bank order in American English
items.meaningCN: 美式英语中的同一票据
items.example: He paid by check in New York.

items.meaning: the place where you pay in a shop
items.example: The queue at the checkout was long.
A blank cheque is a risky gift.
items.exampleCN: 空白支票是份冒险的礼物。

items.meaning: the chess threat to a king
items.exampleCN: eschec 是两种拼写共同的源头。

latinEntries.meaning: a chess threat to the king
latinEntries.example: Eschec became English check and cheque.
latinEntries.exampleCN: eschec 变成英语的 check 与 cheque。

definition_en: to love and care for someone or something deeply, or to keep a hope or a memory in your mind
core_image: 双手捧着一件旧物贴在胸前
scene: 老人把泛黄的照片轻轻夹进书页。She cherished the letter her grandmother had written.
sceneCN: 这里 cherish 指「珍爱」（第 1 个义项：深深爱惜并细心呵护）；句意是她珍爱祖母写的那封信。

senses.title: To love and protect
senses.definition: to love someone or something deeply and to treat it with care
senses.definitionCN: 深深爱着某人或某物，并小心对待
senses.example: He cherished the old watch his father left him.
senses.exampleCN: 他珍爱父亲留给他的那只旧表。
senses.why: The Old French source meant to hold dear, and holding dear easily becomes caring for.
senses.whyCN: 古法语词源意为「视为珍贵」，而视为珍贵很容易变成细心呵护。

senses.title: To keep in the mind
senses.definition: to keep a hope, idea or memory in your mind over a long time
senses.definitionCN: 长时间把某种希望、想法或记忆留在心里
senses.example: She cherished the hope of returning one day.
senses.exampleCN: 她怀着有朝一日回去的希望。
senses.why: What is dear is kept close, so the verb stretched from objects to hopes held inside.
senses.whyCN: 珍贵之物会被收在身边，于是动词从实物扩展到心里怀着的希望。

intro.en: Cherish comes from a Latin adjective meaning dear, through French verbs of holding dear.
intro.cn: cherish 源自拉丁语中表示「珍贵」的形容词，经法语中「视为珍贵」的动词传来。

items.en: Carus meant dear or beloved.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carus 意为珍贵的、被爱的。

items.en: Cher meant dear.
items.cn: 古法语 cher 意为珍贵的。

items.en: Cherir meant to hold someone or something dear.
items.cn: 古法语 cherir 意为把某人或某物视为珍贵。

items.en: Cherish meant to treat with tenderness and care.
items.cn: 英语 cherish 意为温柔小心地对待。

items.en: The verb also means to keep a hope or memory in the mind.
items.cn: 这个动词也指把希望或记忆留在心里。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cher- opening, while the meaning group names strong affection.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cher- 开头，近义组列出强烈的喜爱之情。

entries.definition: a small round red fruit with a stone
loved and valued highly
a picture of a small winged child
to value something very highly
to think that something is important
to love someone very much

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the dear root carus, the -ish verb ending and the hope sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用表示「珍贵」的词根 carus、动词词尾 -ish 以及「怀有」的义项。

normal.en: Cherish hides carus, the Latin word for dear, also seen in charity and caress.
normal.cn: cherish 里藏着拉丁语 carus（珍贵的），charity 与 caress 也含这个词根。

normal.en: The -ish ending makes a verb here, as in finish and punish.
normal.cn: 这里的 -ish 词尾构成动词，如 finish 与 punish。

normal.en: You cherish a person, a gift, a memory or a hope; the object is always dear.
normal.cn: cherish 的宾语可以是人、礼物、记忆或希望，共同点是都很珍贵。

normal.en: Cherished is the common adjective: a cherished friend, a cherished habit.
normal.cn: cherished 是常见形容词：珍爱的朋友、珍视的习惯。

normal.en: The past tense cherished doubles no consonant: cherish, cherished.
normal.cn: 过去式 cherished 不双写辅音：cherish 之后直接加 -ed。

abstract.en: Picture two hands closing around a faded photograph.
abstract.cn: 想象双手把一张褪色照片合在掌心。

abstract.en: Picture a child sleeping with a worn toy under the arm.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子胳膊下夹着一只磨旧的玩具睡去。

abstract.en: Picture a hope kept like a small flame behind cupped hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一点希望像捧在手后的小火苗。

examples.en: They cherished every day they spent together.
examples.cn: 他们珍惜在一起的每一天。

examples.en: He still cherishes the notebook from his first job.
examples.cn: 他仍珍藏着第一份工作时的笔记本。

examples.en: She cherished the hope that the letter would arrive.
examples.cn: 她一直怀着信会寄到的希望。

dict_mnemonic.text: cher 让人想到 cherish 里的「亲爱的」：把心爱之物捧在手心，就是珍爱。

root: 源自拉丁语 carus（珍贵的、亲爱的），经古法语 cher（珍贵）与 cherir（视为珍贵）进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Holding something dear gives the sense of loving care, and a dear thing kept close gives the sense of a hope held in the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 把某物视为珍贵给出「爱惜呵护」的意思，而珍贵之物被收在身边又给出「心里怀着」的意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands holding something old and precious.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手捧着一件旧而珍贵的东西。

branches.en: People and objects receive loving care.
branches.cn: 人与物得到充满爱的呵护。

branches.en: Hopes and memories are kept inside.
branches.cn: 希望与记忆被留在心里。

branches.en: The adjective cherished describes what is loved.
branches.cn: 形容词 cherished 描述被爱惜之物。

branches.en: Both senses turn on the value of the object.
branches.cn: 两个义项都围绕对象的价值。

branches.en: A cherished hope can last for years.
branches.cn: 一个被珍藏的希望可以持续多年。

intro.en: Cherish carries the car- root of dearness into a verb.
intro.cn: cherish 把表示「珍贵」的 car- 词根带进动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin carus and caritas stand behind cherish, charity and caress.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carus 与 caritas 是 cherish、charity 与 caress 的共同来源。

items.meaning: loved and valued in the past
items.example: He cherished that summer for years.
She is cherishing her last weeks at home.
items.exampleCN: 她正珍惜在家的最后几周。

items.example: It is a cherished family custom.
items.exampleCN: 这是一个受珍视的家庭习俗。

items.meaning: kindness shown to those in need
items.example: The old word charity shares the same root.

items.meaning: to touch someone gently and lovingly
items.example: She caressed the sleeping child's hair.
items.exampleCN: 她轻抚睡着的孩子的头发。

latinEntries.example: Carus became Old French cher.
latinEntries.exampleCN: carus 变成古法语 cher。

latinEntries.example: Caritas gave English charity.
latinEntries.exampleCN: caritas 给英语提供了 charity。

definition_en: the front part of the body between the neck and the stomach, or a large strong box with a lid
core_image: 一只带铜锁的木箱，也指人的胸腔
scene: 阁楼里堆着落满灰的旧物。She found a wooden chest full of letters under the window.
sceneCN: 这里 chest 指「箱子」（第 2 个义项：带盖的大型储物箱）；句意是她在窗下找到一只装满信件的木箱。

collocations.phrase: fold one's arms across one's chest

derivatives.zh: 胸部不适的；胸部突出的

senses.title: The front of the body
senses.definition: the front part of the body between the neck and the stomach
senses.definitionCN: 脖子与腹部之间的身体前部
senses.example: He felt a sharp pain in his chest.
senses.exampleCN: 他感到胸口一阵剧痛。
senses.why: The box word was applied to the rib cage, which encloses the heart and lungs like a lid.
senses.whyCN: 表示箱子的词被用到肋骨构成的「胸腔」上，因为它像带盖的容器一样包住心肺。

senses.title: A large strong box
senses.definition: a large strong box with a lid, used for storing things
senses.definitionCN: 带盖的大型坚固储物箱
senses.example: The sailors kept their clothes in a wooden chest.
senses.exampleCN: 水手们把衣服放在一只木箱里。
senses.why: The oldest sense came from Greek and Latin words for a box.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项来自希腊语与拉丁语中表示箱子的词。

senses.title: A piece of furniture with drawers
senses.definition: a piece of furniture with drawers, used for keeping clothes
senses.definitionCN: 带抽屉、用来存放衣物的家具
senses.example: The clean shirts are in the chest of drawers.
senses.exampleCN: 干净的衬衫在五斗柜里。
senses.why: A chest of drawers is a box turned into furniture, so the short name stayed.
senses.whyCN: 五斗柜是把箱子变成家具，简短的名称便保留下来。

intro.en: Chest first meant a box, and only later borrowed the shape for the human rib cage.
intro.cn: chest 最初指箱子，后来才借这个形状指人的胸腔。

items.en: Kiste named a box for storage.
items.cn: 希腊语 kiste 指储物的箱子。

items.en: Cista named a box or a case.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cista 指箱子或匣子。

items.en: Cest named a box with a lid.
items.cn: 古英语 cest 指带盖的箱子。

items.en: The box word was transferred to the rib cage.
items.cn: 表示箱子的词被转用到肋骨围成的胸腔上。

items.en: Chest covers the body, storage boxes and chests of drawers.
items.cn: 如今 chest 涵盖身体部位、储物箱与五斗柜。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- opening, while the meaning group lists containers and body words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 开头，近义组列出容器与身体部位词。

entries.definition: a board game of kings and queens
entries.definitionCN: 以国王与王后为棋子的棋盘游戏

entries.definition: the side of the face below the eye
a solid food made from milk
entries.definitionCN: 用牛奶制成的固体食品

entries.definition: a container with stiff sides and a lid
a large strong case for travel
a container made for one kind of thing
entries.definitionCN: 为某类物品制作的容器

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the box origin, the container shape of the body and the drawers idiom.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「箱子」来源、身体的容器形状以及五斗柜的说法。

normal.en: Chest began as a box, and the ribs still make a box around the heart.
normal.cn: chest 本是箱子，而肋骨至今仍在心脏周围围成一只箱子。

normal.en: A chest of drawers is a box grown legs and handles.
normal.cn: chest of drawers 就是长出腿和把手的箱子。

normal.en: Get it off your chest: say the worry out loud and feel lighter.
normal.cn: get it off your chest：把心事说出来，就会轻松一些。

normal.en: Chest pain, chest cold, chest X-ray: medical phrases keep the body sense.
normal.cn: chest pain、chest cold、chest X-ray，这些医学搭配保留身体义。

normal.en: The plural chests adds an s to both the box and the body.
normal.cn: 复数 chests 对箱子和胸部同样只加 s。

abstract.en: Picture a brass lock catching light on an old wooden lid.
abstract.cn: 想象旧木箱盖上铜锁反着光。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressed flat against a heartbeat.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手平放在跳动的心口。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer sliding open on folded shirts.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉滑开，露出叠好的衬衫。

examples.en: The nurse listened to his chest and took notes.
examples.cn: 护士听了他的胸部，做了记录。

examples.en: An old chest stood at the foot of the bed.
examples.cn: 床脚放着一只旧箱子。

examples.en: She keeps her winter clothes in the chest of drawers.
examples.cn: 她把冬衣放在五斗柜里。

dict_mnemonic.text: chest 像一只箱子：木箱装东西，胸腔装心肺，抽屉柜装衣服。

root: 源自希腊语 kiste（箱子），经拉丁语 cista 与古英语 cest 进入英语，十六世纪起兼指胸腔。

sensesIntro.en: The stored box is the oldest sense, the body borrowed its shape, and the furniture borrowed its name.
sensesIntro.cn: 储物箱是最古老义项，身体借用了它的形状，家具又借用了它的名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lidded container that holds something precious inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只带盖、内装贵重之物的容器。

branches.en: The body sense names the rib cage.
branches.cn: 身体义项指肋骨围成的胸腔。

branches.en: The box sense keeps the lid and the lock.
branches.cn: 箱子义项保留盖与锁。

branches.en: The furniture sense adds drawers to the box.
branches.cn: 家具义项给箱子添上抽屉。

branches.en: Both senses share the container image.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享容器意象。

branches.en: A chest of drawers is a box made for a bedroom.
branches.cn: 五斗柜是为卧室改造的箱子。

intro.en: Chest stays one short stem through its plural and its two derivatives.
intro.cn: chest 在复数与两个派生词中保持同一个短词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin cista, a box, comes from Greek kiste and gives English chest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cista（箱子）来自希腊语 kiste，并给出英语的 chest。

items.meaning: the body front or a strong box

items.example: Two chests stood in the hall.
The child had a chesty cough.

items.meaning: as much as a chest holds
items.example: A chestful of old maps was found.
items.exampleCN: 发现了满满一箱旧地图。

items.example: The drawer stuck in damp weather.
items.exampleCN: 潮湿天气里抽屉会卡住。

items.meaning: one of the curved bones of the chest

items.exampleCN: cista 变成古英语的 cest。

latinEntries.example: Cista is the direct source of chest.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cista 是 chest 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Kiste is the oldest layer of the word.
latinEntries.exampleCN: kiste 是这个词最古老的一层。

definition_en: to crush food with the teeth before swallowing, or to think about something again and again
core_image: 闭着嘴慢慢咀嚼的人
scene: 食堂里人声嘈杂，盘子碰得叮当响。He chewed each mouthful slowly and said nothing.
sceneCN: 这里 chew 指「咀嚼」（第 1 个义项：用牙齿反复嚼碎食物）；句意是他每一口都慢慢咀嚼，什么也没说。

senses.title: To crush food with the teeth
senses.definition: to break food into small pieces with the teeth before swallowing
senses.definitionCN: 吞咽之前用牙齿把食物弄碎
senses.example: Chew your food before you swallow it.
senses.exampleCN: 吞下去之前先把食物嚼碎。
senses.why: The Old English verb named the work of the jaws, and that physical sense has never changed.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词本指颌部的动作，这一身体义从未改变。

senses.title: To think something over
senses.definition: to consider an idea or a problem slowly and repeatedly
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢而反复地思考某个想法或问题
senses.example: He chewed over the offer for a whole week.
senses.exampleCN: 他把这个提议反复琢磨了整整一周。
senses.why: Turning food in the mouth became a picture for turning an idea in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 嘴里翻动食物，成了脑中翻动想法的比喻。

intro.en: Chew is an old English verb that has kept its bodily meaning for a thousand years.
intro.cn: chew 是一个古英语动词，一千年间一直保留着身体动作的含义。

items.en: Kewwan meant to chew or to crush with the teeth.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 kewwan 意为咀嚼或用牙弄碎。

items.en: Ceowan named the action of the jaws on food.
items.cn: 古英语 ceowan 指颌部对食物的动作。

items.en: Chewen kept the plain food sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 chewen 保留单纯的食物义。

items.en: The phrase chew over stretched the action to thinking.
items.cn: chew over 这一说法把动作延伸到思考。

items.en: Chewy and chewing gum joined the family later.
items.cn: chewy 与 chewing gum 后来加入这个词族。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- opening, while the meaning group lists ways of biting food.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 开头，近义组列出咬食物的各种方式。

entries.definition: the side of the face below the eye
a solid food made from milk
entries.definitionCN: 用牛奶制成的固体食品

entries.definition: the part of the face below the mouth
to cut into something with the teeth
to keep biting something hard
to eat something steadily and noisily

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the jaw relatives, the chew over idiom and the chewy adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用颌部同源词、chew over 习语以及形容词 chewy。

normal.en: Chew and cheek come from the same jaw area: one is the action, the other the flesh.
normal.cn: chew 与 cheek 都出自颌部：一个是动作，一个是皮肉。

normal.en: Chew over means to turn a problem in the mind as if it were food.
normal.cn: chew over 意为把问题当食物一样在脑子里翻来覆去。

normal.en: Chewy describes meat or candy that resists the teeth.
normal.cn: chewy 形容需要用牙使劲的肉或糖。

normal.en: The past tense is simply chewed, with no doubled consonant.
normal.cn: 过去式就是 chewed，辅音不双写。

normal.en: Chewing gum keeps the mouth busy without any food.
normal.cn: chewing gum 让嘴一直动着，却不是在吃东西。

abstract.en: Picture a man eating slowly while the table talks around him.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人慢慢吃着，桌边的人都在说话。

abstract.en: Picture a pen top flattened by nervous teeth.
abstract.cn: 想象笔帽被紧张的牙咬扁。

abstract.en: Picture a cow's jaw moving in a steady circle.
abstract.cn: 想象牛的下颌一圈圈不停地动。

examples.en: The meat was too tough to chew.
examples.cn: 这肉太硬，嚼不动。

examples.en: She chewed her sandwich while reading the report.
examples.cn: 她一边嚼三明治一边看报告。

examples.en: Give him time to chew over the plan.
examples.cn: 给他时间反复考虑这个计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: chew 与 cheek 同源：动的是下巴和脸颊，嚼的是嘴里的东西。

root: 源自日耳曼语 kewwan（咀嚼），古英语作 ceowan，中古英语作 chewen，身体义沿用至今。

sensesIntro.en: The teeth crushing food gives the physical sense, and the same turning motion gives the mental sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 牙齿弄碎食物给出身体义，而同样的翻动动作给出心理义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: teeth working slowly on a mouthful of food.
core.cn: 核心意象：牙齿慢慢对付一口食物。

branches.en: Food is crushed before it is swallowed.
branches.cn: 食物在吞下之前被嚼碎。

branches.en: An idea is turned over the same way.
branches.cn: 一个想法也以同样方式被反复翻动。

branches.en: Chewy food resists the teeth for a while.
branches.cn: 有嚼劲的食物会让牙齿多费些力。

branches.en: Both senses share a slow repeated motion.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享缓慢重复的动作。

branches.en: Chew over keeps the food picture in the mind.
branches.cn: chew over 把食物的画面留在脑中。

intro.en: Chew has a small family built from one Old English stem.
intro.cn: chew 由一个古英语词干构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, not Latin, so the oldest layers are English and Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，最古老的层次是英语与日耳曼语。

items.meaning: to crush food with the teeth

items.example: He chews on the left side only.
The bread was warm and chewy.
He bought a pack of chewing gum.
His cheek moved as he chewed.

latinEntries.example: Kewwan became Old English ceowan.

senses.title: The farm bird

senses.title: The meat as food

senses.title: A timid person

definition_en: the leader of a group or an organization, or most important and highest in rank
core_image: 站在队伍最前面的那个人
scene: 会议桌两端坐满了人，屋里渐渐安静。The chief of the village spoke last and everyone listened.
sceneCN: 这里 chief 指「首领」（第 1 个义项：群体或组织的领导者）；句意是村里的首领最后发言，所有人都在听。

senses.title: The leader of a group
senses.definition: the person who leads a group, a tribe or an organization
senses.definitionCN: 领导群体、部落或组织的人
senses.example: The village chief settled the dispute himself.
senses.exampleCN: 村长亲自解决了这场争端。
senses.why: The Latin word for head gave the name of the person at the head of a body of people.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示「头」的词，给出了站在一群人最前面那个人的称呼。

senses.title: Most important
senses.definition: most important among several things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 同类事物中最重要的
senses.example: The chief reason for the delay was the weather.
senses.exampleCN: 延误的主要原因是天气。
senses.why: The head is the top of the body, so the adjective came to mean topmost in importance.
senses.whyCN: 头是身体的顶端，因此形容词表示重要性上位居最高。

senses.title: Highest in rank
senses.definition: holding the highest position in a profession or an office
senses.definitionCN: 在某行业或机构中居于最高职位的
senses.example: She was appointed chief engineer of the project.
senses.exampleCN: 她被任命为该项目的总工程师。
senses.why: Rank is pictured as height, so the head word marks the top post in a title.
senses.whyCN: 等级被想象成高低，因此这个「头」词标记出头衔中的最高职位。

intro.en: Chief is the Latin word for head, carried through French into English.
intro.cn: chief 是拉丁语中表示「头」的词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Caput meant the head of a person or an animal.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caput 指人或动物的头。

items.en: Chief meant the head, both of a body and of a group.
items.cn: 古法语 chief 既指身体的头，也指群体的头。

items.en: Chief named the leading person of a household or a band.
items.cn: 英语 chief 指家庭或队伍中的领头人。

items.en: The same form began to work as an adjective meaning principal.
items.cn: 同一形式开始作形容词，意为首要的。

items.en: Chief covers leaders, top posts and the most important reason.
items.cn: 如今 chief 涵盖首领、最高职位与最重要的理由。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same long vowel or the same origin, while the meaning group names leaders.
note.cn: 形近组共享相同的长元音或同一来源，近义组列出领导者。

a community ruled by a chief

the person in charge of a group

normal.en: Chief and chef are twins: the French form became the cook, the English one the leader.
normal.cn: chief 与 chef 是一对双胞胎：法语形式成了厨师，英语形式成了首领。

normal.en: Chief hides caput, the Latin head, also seen in capital and captain.
normal.cn: chief 里藏着拉丁语「头」caput，capital 与 captain 也含这个词根。

normal.en: A chief is at the head of people; a chief reason is at the head of a list.
normal.cn: chief 是人前的头，也是理由清单上的头。

normal.en: The plural chiefs simply adds an s after two consonants.
normal.cn: 复数 chiefs 只需在词尾加 s。

normal.en: Editor in chief puts the head word after the job, a common newspaper title.
normal.cn: editor in chief 把「头」词放在职务之后，是常见的报纸头衔。

abstract.en: Picture one figure standing a step ahead of a long line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在长队前面半步。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised to quiet a whole hall.

abstract.en: Picture a name plate reading chief engineer on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上放着一块写着总工程师的名牌。

examples.en: The chief called the meeting to order.

examples.en: Safety is our chief concern.

sensesIntro.en: The head of a body of people gives the leader, and the head as the topmost part gives both the important and the highest-ranked senses.
sensesIntro.cn: 一群人中的「头」给出首领义，而作为最顶端的「头」给出「主要」与「最高职位」两个义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the head of a body, human or social.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个身体或一个群体的「头」。

branches.en: The leader sense names a person.
branches.cn: 首领义项指一个人。

branches.en: The important sense ranks reasons and aims.
branches.cn: 主要义项给理由与目标排序。

branches.en: The rank sense builds titles such as chief engineer.
branches.cn: 职位义项构成总工程师这类头衔。

branches.en: A chief holds the chief post.

branches.en: Both adjective senses place something at the top.

latinIntro.en: Latin caput, the head, also gives capital, captain and the French chef.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput（头）也给出 capital、captain 以及法语的 chef。

definition_en: a young human being, or a son or daughter of any age

scene: 公园长椅旁，一个小身影蹲下来看地面。The child watched the ants for almost an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 child 指「儿童」（第 1 个义项：年幼的人）；句意是那个孩子看蚂蚁看了将近一小时。

senses.title: A young person
senses.definition: a human being who is not yet an adult
senses.definitionCN: 尚未成年的人
senses.example: Every child in the class received a book.
senses.exampleCN: 班上每个孩子都得到了一本书。
senses.why: The Old English word named a young person, and that sense has stayed at the centre.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词指年幼的人，这一义项始终居于中心。

senses.title: A son or daughter
senses.definition: a son or a daughter of any age, seen from the parent's side
senses.definitionCN: 从父母角度看，任何年龄的儿子或女儿
senses.example: They have three children, all grown up.
senses.exampleCN: 他们有三个孩子，都已成年。
senses.why: A parent's relation to offspring lasts for life, so the word ignores age.
senses.whyCN: 父母与子女的关系终身存在，因此这个词不再管年龄。

senses.title: A product of its time
senses.definition: something that is produced by a particular period or influence
senses.definitionCN: 由某个时期或某种影响产生的事物
senses.example: The novel is a child of the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说是上个世纪的产物。
senses.why: Something produced is pictured as born, so child became a metaphor for a product.
senses.whyCN: 被产生出来的东西被想象成「出生」，于是 child 成了产物的比喻。

intro.en: Child is an old English word, and its plural children is an old double plural.

items.en: A root kel- named the womb and the young born from it.

items.en: Cild meant a fetus or a young person.

items.en: The plural cildru appeared beside the singular.
items.cn: 复数形式 cildru 与单数形式并存。

items.en: Children added -en to an older plural, a double plural.
items.cn: children 在旧复数后加了 -en，形成双重复数。

items.en: Child covers young people, offspring of any age and products of a period.

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- and -ild shape, while the meaning group names young people.
