items.en: Childhood fixed the sense of the whole period of being young.
items.cn: childhood 固定为「整个年幼时期」的意思。

items.en: The word also describes the early stage of an industry or an idea.
items.cn: 这个词也用来描述行业或观念的早期阶段。

note.en: The look-alike group grows from child, while the meaning group names periods of early life.
note.cn: 形近组由 child 派生，近义组列出生命的早期阶段。

entries.definition: a young person
silly in the way of a child
more than one child
the period when someone is young
the earliest period of life
the time when someone is a boy

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -hood period suffix and the parallel words adulthood and manhood.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用表示时期的 -hood 后缀以及 adulthood、manhood 这类平行词。

normal.en: Childhood is child plus -hood, the same ending that gives adulthood and manhood.
normal.cn: childhood 是 child 加 -hood，adulthood 与 manhood 也用这个结尾。

normal.en: The suffix -hood names a state or a span of time, never a place.
normal.cn: 后缀 -hood 表示状态或一段时间，从不表示地点。

normal.en: Childhood is uncountable, so you say a happy childhood, not happy childhoods.
normal.cn: childhood 不可数，所以说 a happy childhood，而不用复数。

normal.en: Childhood memories are the scenes that stay after the years go.
normal.cn: childhood memories 是岁月过去后仍留着的画面。

normal.en: An industry in its childhood is young and still experimenting.
normal.cn: 处在 childhood 的行业很年轻，仍在摸索。

abstract.en: Picture a photo album open on a dusty floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一本相册摊在落灰的地板上。

abstract.en: Picture a river town seen from a child's height.
abstract.cn: 想象从孩子的高度看河边小镇。

abstract.en: Picture a small bicycle leaning against a wall for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆小自行车靠墙放了很多年。

examples.en: She had a quiet childhood in the countryside.
examples.cn: 她在乡下度过了安静的童年。

examples.en: Childhood memories of that kitchen still comfort him.
examples.cn: 那间厨房的童年记忆至今让他安心。

examples.en: Electric cars were still in their childhood a decade ago.
examples.cn: 十年前电动汽车还处在萌芽阶段。

dict_mnemonic.text: child 加 -hood（表示时期）：当孩子的那些年，就是童年。

root: 由古英语 cild（幼者）加本土后缀 -hood（状态、时期，源自古英语 -had）构成。

sensesIntro.en: The suffix turns a person into a period, and any young thing can borrow that period as a metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个后缀把人变成一个时期，而任何新生事物都能借这段时期作比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a span of years seen through a child's eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：透过孩子的眼睛看到的一段岁月。

branches.en: The personal sense covers the years of youth.
branches.cn: 个人义项涵盖年少的岁月。

branches.en: The metaphor sense describes young industries.
branches.cn: 比喻义项描述年轻的行业。

branches.en: Childhood friends are friends from those years.
branches.cn: childhood friends 是那段岁月结识的朋友。

branches.en: Both senses share the image of an early beginning.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「早期开端」的意象。

branches.en: A science in its childhood still makes basic mistakes.
branches.cn: 处于童年期的科学仍会犯基本错误。

intro.en: Childhood is a clean compound of a noun and a period suffix.
intro.cn: childhood 是名词与时期后缀的清晰组合。

latinIntro.en: Neither part is Latin: child is Germanic and -hood comes from Old English -had.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都不是拉丁语：child 属日耳曼语，-hood 来自古英语 -had。

items.meaning: the period of being a child
items.exampleCN: 他的童年塑造了他的品味。

items.example: He has a childlike trust in people.
items.exampleCN: 他对人有种孩子般天真的信任。

items.meaning: the period of being an adult
the state of being a man

latinEntries.example: Cild is the first half of childhood.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cild 是 childhood 的前半。

latinEntries.example: The suffix -had became modern -hood.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 后缀 -had 变成现代的 -hood。

definition_zh: 寒意；风寒；使变冷；使寒心
definition_en: a cold feeling, a mild illness caused by cold, or to make something cold
core_image: 打开冰箱门时扑面而来的白气
scene: 夜里风从窗缝里钻进来。A chill ran down his back when the door creaked open.
sceneCN: 这里 chill 指「寒意」（第 1 个义项：突然感到的一阵冷）；句意是门吱呀一开，一股寒意顺着他的背脊而下。

collocations.phrase: send a chill down one's spine

senses.title: A feeling of cold
senses.definition: a sudden cold feeling in the air or in the body
senses.definitionCN: 空气里或身体上突然感到的冷
senses.example: There was a chill in the room before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前屋里有一股寒意。
senses.why: The Old English word for cold named the sensation itself, and that sense remains the core.
senses.whyCN: 古英语中表示冷的词本指这种感觉本身，这一义项始终是核心。

senses.title: To make something cold
senses.definition: to make food or drink cold without freezing it
senses.definitionCN: 让食物或饮料变冷但不结冰
senses.example: Chill the soup for an hour before serving.
senses.exampleCN: 上桌前把汤冰一小时。
senses.why: The noun became a verb for causing the sensation in an object.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，表示为物体制造这种感觉。

senses.title: To frighten or discourage
senses.definition: to make someone feel fear or a sudden loss of hope
senses.definitionCN: 让人感到恐惧或突然失去希望
senses.example: The empty streets chilled the visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 空荡的街道让来访者心里发凉。
senses.why: Fear is felt as cold running down the back, so the cold word moved into emotion.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧常被感觉为背上一阵冷，于是表示冷的词转入情绪。

intro.en: Chill is an old English word for cold that later took on fear and cooling.
intro.cn: chill 是表示寒冷的一个古英语词，后来兼指恐惧与冷却。

items.en: Kal- named cold and coldness.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词根 kal- 指冷与寒冷。

items.en: Ciele named a cold feeling or a cold illness.
items.cn: 古英语 ciele 指寒冷的感觉或受寒之病。

items.en: Chil kept the sense of a shivering cold.
items.cn: 中古英语 chil 保留「冷得发抖」的意思。

items.en: The noun became a verb meaning to make cold.
items.cn: 名词转为动词，意为使变冷。

items.en: Chill also means to frighten, and chill out means to relax.
items.cn: 如今 chill 也指使人恐惧，而 chill out 意为放松。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- and short i, while the meaning group names cold and fear.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 与短元音 i，近义组列出寒冷与恐惧。

entries.definition: a young person
a small hot pepper
rather cold in a unpleasant way
a low temperature or the feeling of it
the quality of being cold
to become hard and solid with cold

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the cold root, the shiver image and the chill out idiom.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「冷」词根、发抖的画面以及 chill out 习语。

normal.en: Chill and chilly share one root: chill is the feeling, chilly is the weather.
normal.cn: chill 与 chilly 同根：chill 是感觉，chilly 是天气。

normal.en: Catch a chill is the old phrase for catching a cold.
normal.cn: catch a chill 是「着凉」的旧说法。

normal.en: A chill down the spine mixes cold and fear in one image.
normal.cn: a chill down the spine 把寒冷与恐惧合在一幅画面里。

normal.en: To chill drinks is to cool them; to chill a person is to frighten them.
normal.cn: chill drinks 是让饮料变冷，chill a person 是让人心里发凉。

normal.en: Chill out means relax, a modern and very common use.
normal.cn: chill out 意为放松，是现代极其常见的用法。

abstract.en: Picture white mist rolling out of an open freezer.
abstract.cn: 想象白气从打开冰柜里滚出来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand rubbing its arms in a cold corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在寒冷的走廊里搓着胳膊。

abstract.en: Picture a hair rising on the back of a neck.
abstract.cn: 想象后颈上汗毛竖起。

examples.en: A chill came through the open window.
examples.cn: 一阵寒意从敞开的窗子透进来。

examples.en: They chilled the wine before dinner.
examples.cn: 他们在晚餐前把酒冰了一下。

examples.en: The ghost story chilled the whole room.
examples.cn: 那个鬼故事让整个房间的人都发冷。

dict_mnemonic.text: chill 与 chilly 同根：身上一阵冷是 chill，外面冷冷的天气是 chilly。

root: 源自古英语 ciele（寒冷、受寒），属日耳曼语词根 kal-（冷），后引申出「使冷却」与「使恐惧」。

sensesIntro.en: The cold sensation is the base, causing cold in an object gives the verb, and cold inside the body gives fear.
sensesIntro.cn: 寒冷的感觉是基础，让物体变冷给出动词义，而体内的冷给出恐惧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sudden cold that makes the skin tighten.
core.cn: 核心意象：一阵让皮肤收紧的骤冷。

branches.en: The noun names air or body cold.
branches.cn: 名词义项指空气或身体上的冷。

branches.en: The verb cools drinks and food.
branches.cn: 动词义项让饮料与食物变凉。

branches.en: The fear sense chills a person.
branches.cn: 恐惧义项让人心里发冷。

branches.en: Both deal with temperature only.
branches.cn: 两者只涉及温度。

branches.en: Cold becomes a picture for fright.
branches.cn: 冷成了恐惧的画面。

intro.en: Chill expands into an adjective and two participles with little change of stem.
intro.cn: chill 扩展出形容词与两个分词，词干几乎不变。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the cold root kal- also lies behind cool.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属日耳曼语，表示冷的词根 kal- 也藏在 cool 之后。

items.example: The wind was chilling his hands.
Chilled water was on the table.
The chiller keeps the milk fresh.
items.exampleCN: 冷却机让牛奶保持新鲜。

latinEntries.example: Ciele is the oldest form of chill.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ciele 是 chill 最古老的形式。

definition_en: the part of the face below the mouth and above the neck
core_image: 抬起下巴时露出的一道侧面轮廓
scene: 摄影师让那人把头抬高一点。He rested his chin on his hand and looked out of the window.
sceneCN: 这里 chin 指「下巴」（第 1 个义项：嘴下方的面部部位）；句意是他用手托着下巴望向窗外。

derivatives.zh: 下巴不明显的；意志薄弱的

senses.title: The part below the mouth
senses.definition: the part of the face that lies below the mouth and above the neck
senses.definitionCN: 位于嘴下方、颈部上方的面部部位
senses.example: He cut his chin while shaving.
senses.exampleCN: 他刮胡子时刮伤了下巴。
senses.why: The Old English word named the lower jaw, and the sense has stayed bodily and stable.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词指下颌，这一义项始终是身体部位且非常稳定。

senses.title: Courage to take a blow
senses.definition: the strength to accept a hard blow or criticism without giving up
senses.definitionCN: 承受重击或批评而不放弃的韧劲
senses.example: She took the bad news on the chin and kept working.
senses.exampleCN: 她默默承受了坏消息，继续工作。
senses.why: A punch lands on the chin, so the word came to stand for enduring a hit.
senses.whyCN: 拳头常打在下巴上，于是这个词被用来表示承受一击。

intro.en: Chin is an old Germanic word for the lower jaw that English has never replaced.
intro.cn: chin 是一个古老的日耳曼语词，指下颌，英语从未换掉它。

items.en: Kinnuz named the jaw or the chin.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 kinnuz 指颌或下巴。

items.en: Cin named the lower jaw and the chin.
items.cn: 古英语 cin 指下颌与下巴。

items.en: Chin settled as the everyday word for the feature.
items.cn: 中古英语 chin 定型为这个部位的日常词。

items.en: Sports talk gave chin the sense of taking a punch.
items.cn: 体育谈话让 chin 带上「挨拳」的意思。

items.en: Chin covers the body part and a group of courage idioms.
items.cn: 如今 chin 既指身体部位，也构成一组表示韧劲的习语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- and short i, while the meaning group names the lower face.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 与短元音 i，近义组列出面部下方的部位。

entries.definition: a cold feeling
the side of the face below the eye
having little width or fat
either of the bones that hold the teeth
the lower part of a person's cheek
the outline of the lower jaw

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the jaw relatives, the chin up idiom and the double chin picture.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用颌部相关词、chin up 习语以及双下巴的画面。

normal.en: Chin and jaw sit side by side: the chin is the front point, the jaw the whole bone.
normal.cn: chin 与 jaw 相邻：chin 是前面的尖角，jaw 是整块骨。

normal.en: Keep your chin up: lift the head and the mood rises with it.
normal.cn: keep your chin up：把头抬起，心情也跟着上去。

normal.en: A double chin is a second curve under the first.
normal.cn: 双下巴就是第一道曲线下面又多出一道。

normal.en: Take it on the chin means to accept a hit without complaining.
normal.cn: take it on the chin 意为挨了打也不抱怨。

normal.en: The plural chins is regular, though the feature usually appears once.
normal.cn: 复数 chins 变化规则，尽管这个部位通常只有一个。

abstract.en: Picture a head tilted up toward a camera.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头朝相机微微抬起。

abstract.en: Picture a hand supporting a tired face.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手托着疲惫的脸。

abstract.en: Picture a boxer lifting his head after a hard round.
abstract.cn: 想象拳手在艰苦的一回合后抬起头。

examples.en: A drop of rain ran off his chin.
examples.cn: 一滴雨从他的下巴滑落。

examples.en: She rested her chin on her folded hands.
examples.cn: 她把下巴搁在交叠的手上。

examples.en: He took the failure on the chin and tried again.
examples.cn: 他默默承受失败，又重新尝试。

dict_mnemonic.text: chin 和 cheek 都在脸上：cheek 在脸侧，chin 在脸的最下端。

root: 源自日耳曼语 kinnuz（颌、下巴），古英语作 cin，中古英语定型为 chin。

sensesIntro.en: The bodily feature is the literal sense, and the place where a punch lands gives the sense of endurance.
sensesIntro.cn: 面部部位是字面义，而拳头落下的位置给出「承受」的义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the small point at the bottom of a face.
core.cn: 核心意象：脸的最下端那个小小尖角。

branches.en: The body sense names the feature itself.
branches.cn: 身体义项指这个部位本身。

branches.en: The courage sense lives in fixed phrases.
branches.cn: 韧劲义项存在于固定说法中。

branches.en: A double chin is described with the same word.
branches.cn: 双下巴同样用这个词描述。

branches.en: Both senses are tied to the same small area.
branches.cn: 两个义项都系于同一小块部位。

branches.en: Taking it on the chin means showing no complaint.
branches.cn: take it on the chin 意为不抱怨地承受。

intro.en: Chin is a short stem with only a few derived forms.
intro.cn: chin 是个短词干，派生形式不多。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, with no Latin ancestor for this everyday word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属日耳曼语，这个日常词没有拉丁语祖先。

items.example: His chin was covered in foam.
The cartoon babies had huge chins.
items.exampleCN: 卡通婴儿的下巴特别大。

items.example: The portrait showed a chinless profile.
items.exampleCN: 画像里是一张下巴不明显的侧脸。

items.example: He fastened the chinstrap of his helmet.

items.meaning: the bone that holds the teeth
items.example: His jaw was tight with anger.
A bruise spread across his cheek.

items.meaning: the opening for eating and speaking
items.example: The mouth sits above the chin.

items.exampleCN: kinnuz 变成古英语的 cin。

latinEntries.example: Kinnuz is the oldest layer of chin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: kinnuz 是 chin 最古老的一层。

definition_en: a small piece broken off something, a thin fried piece of potato, or a tiny electronic circuit
core_image: 一小块从木头边缘崩落的薄片
scene: 木匠的工作台上散着一层薄木片。He swept the wood chips into a small pile.
sceneCN: 这里 chip 指「碎片」（第 1 个义项：从整块上崩下的小片）；句意是他把木屑扫成一小堆。

senses.title: A small broken piece
senses.definition: a small piece that has broken off a hard material
senses.definitionCN: 从硬质材料上崩落的小片
senses.example: A chip of stone flew up from the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一小块石头从路面飞起来。
senses.why: The Old English word named a piece of wood, and the sense widened to any broken fragment.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词指一小片木头，后来扩展到任何碎裂的片段。

senses.title: A fried potato slice
senses.definition: a thin piece of potato fried until crisp or golden
senses.definitionCN: 切成薄片、炸至酥脆或金黄的土豆
senses.example: The children shared a bag of chips.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们分吃了一袋薯片。
senses.why: A slice of potato looks like a wood chip, so the same word was borrowed for food.
senses.whyCN: 一片土豆看起来像木片，于是同一个词被借去指食物。

senses.title: A tiny electronic circuit
senses.definition: a very small piece of silicon carrying an electronic circuit
senses.definitionCN: 承载电子电路的一小片硅
senses.example: The new chip runs twice as fast.
senses.exampleCN: 新芯片的运行速度是原来的两倍。
senses.why: A silicon wafer is cut into small pieces, and each piece kept the name chip.
senses.whyCN: 硅片被切成小块，每一块都沿用了 chip 这个名字。

intro.en: Chip began as a piece of wood and spread to food and then to electronics.
intro.cn: chip 起初指一小片木头，后来扩展到食物，再扩展到电子元件。

items.en: Cipp named a small piece of wood.
items.cn: 古英语 cipp 指一小片木头。

items.en: Chip kept the wood sense and added any broken fragment.
items.cn: 中古英语 chip 保留木片义，又添上任何碎裂片段的意思。

items.en: Chips came to name slices of fried potato.
items.cn: chips 开始指炸土豆片。

items.en: The word was applied to a tiny electronic circuit.
items.cn: 这个词被用到微型电子电路上。

items.en: Chip covers fragments, fried food and computer hardware.
items.cn: 如今 chip 涵盖碎片、油炸食品与计算机硬件。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- and short i, while the meaning group names fragments and small parts.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 与短元音 i，近义组列出碎片与小部件。

entries.definition: the part of the face below the mouth
to cut something with quick heavy blows
entries.definitionCN: 用快速有力的动作砍切

entries.definition: a small African ape
a small part broken from something
entries.definitionCN: 从某物上碎下的一小部分

entries.definition: a thin flat piece cut from something
a very small electronic circuit

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the wood origin, the fried potato sense and the silicon chip.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用木头来源、炸土豆义以及硅芯片。

normal.en: A chip is what flies off when an axe meets wood.
normal.cn: chip 就是斧头砍到木头时飞出来的那一小片。

normal.en: A potato sliced thin looks just like a wood chip, so the food took the name.
normal.cn: 切薄的土豆像极了木片，于是食物也用了这个名字。

normal.en: A computer chip is also a small cut piece, this time of silicon.
normal.cn: 计算机芯片同样是一小块切下来的东西，只不过材料是硅。

normal.en: Chip in means to add your share, money or words.
normal.cn: chip in 意为添上自己那一份，无论是钱还是话。

normal.en: The past tense chipped doubles the p before -ed.
normal.cn: 过去式 chipped 在 -ed 前双写 p。

abstract.en: Picture a pale curl of wood falling from a plane.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷浅色木屑从刨子上落下。

abstract.en: Picture a crisp golden slice lifted from hot oil.
abstract.cn: 想象一片金黄脆片从热油里被捞起。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny square of silicon held by tweezers.
abstract.cn: 想象镊子夹着一小片方形硅片。

examples.en: A chip broke off the edge of the cup.
examples.cn: 杯子边缘崩掉了一小块。

examples.en: He ordered fish and chips at the corner shop.
examples.cn: 他在街角小店点了炸鱼薯条。

examples.en: Every phone contains several chips.
examples.cn: 每部手机里都有好几块芯片。

dict_mnemonic.text: chip 就像砍木头崩下的小片：木片、薯片、芯片，都是「一小片」。

root: 源自古英语 cipp（一小片木头），属日耳曼语；后扩展指碎片、油炸土豆片与硅芯片。

sensesIntro.en: A broken wood piece is the base, a potato slice borrows the shape, and a cut silicon square borrows the size.
sensesIntro.cn: 崩落的木片是基础，土豆片借了它的形状，切下的硅片借了它的小。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small piece flying off a hard edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：从硬物边缘飞下的一小片。

branches.en: The fragment sense covers stone and wood.
branches.cn: 碎片义项涵盖石头与木头。

branches.en: The food sense is a thin fried slice.
branches.cn: 食物义项指薄薄的油炸片。

branches.en: The technology sense is a cut silicon square.
branches.cn: 技术义项指切下的方形硅片。

branches.en: Both senses share a small flat shape.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享小而扁的形状。

branches.en: Food and hardware are both counted in chips.
branches.cn: 食物与硬件都用 chips 来计数。

intro.en: Chip stays one short stem across its plural, verb forms and compounds.
intro.cn: chip 在复数、动词形式与复合词中保持同一个短词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, with no Latin source for this small word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属日耳曼语，这个小词没有拉丁语来源。

items.example: A chip flew off the stone.

items.meaning: many small pieces or portions of food

items.example: He chipped the edge of the plate.
items.exampleCN: 他把盘子边缘磕出了缺口。

items.example: The ice was chipping under the axe.
She drank from a chipped cup.
items.exampleCN: 她用一只缺口杯子喝水。

items.meaning: board made of pressed wood chips
items.example: The shelf is made of chipboard.
items.exampleCN: 这个架子是刨花板做的。
微芯片改变了计算技术。

items.example: Cipp is the oldest form of chip.
items.exampleCN: cipp 是 chip 最古老的形式。

latinEntries.example: Cipp became modern chip.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cipp 变成现代的 chip。
